title: 5f-Akb48

attribution.author: Josie Kins
attribution.text: Forked from Subjective Effect Documentation work by Josie Kins, September 2015.

notes.overview: Effects vary widely by individual, dose, and context.

effects.name: Anxiety
effects.description: In comparison to other cannabinoids, this compound is particularly prone to inducing feelings of anxiety and it should therefore be avoided by people who are particularly prone to this state of mind.

effects.name: Spontaneous tactile sensations
effects.description: The body high of 5F-AKB-48 can be described as a sharp, uncomfortable, all-encompassing, electric tingling sensation that spreads over the body after initial ingestion. It maintains a consistent presence that quickly rises with the onset and hits its limit once the peak has been reached before immediately dissipating.

effects.name: Motor control loss
effects.description: This substance causes a partial to moderate suppression of motor control which intensifies proportional to dose, but rarely results in a complete inability to walk and perform basic movements.

effects.name: Appetite enhancement
effects.description: As with many other cannabinoids, 5F-AKB-48 causes an increase in appetite, known colloquially as "the munchies" in popular American and United Kingdom culture. Clinical studies and survey data have found that cannabis increases food enjoyment and interest in food. This is thought to be due to the way in which endocannabinoids in the hypothalamus activate cannabinoid receptors that are responsible for maintaining food intake.

effects.name: Pain relief
effects.description: Cannabinoids have been clinically demonstrated to provide pain relief via agonism of cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2, which extends to synthetic cannabinoid receptor agonists.

effects.name: Perception of increased weight or Perception of decreased weight
Dehydration
effects.description: This is known colloquially as "cotton mouth" in popular American and United Kingdom culture.
